accepted.reason: GPT-6.2 Astra is OpenAI's first external model at its High AI Self-Improvement threshold, and the release connects that tier to isolation, monitoring, staged access, and workload-stop infrastructure. Mixed external evaluations, Tier 1 loss-of-control assessment, blocker omissions, and simulation limits keep the signal bounded.

GitHub's MDASH pilot materially strengthens an existing structural signal with a candidate-to-report-to-fix-to-release funnel and explicit researcher effort. Updating the existing URL avoids duplication and keeps raw scanner volume separate from remediation outcomes.

Microsoft, Entra, and GitHub extend the existing workforce-identity story into cross-platform registration, sponsorship, activity evidence, lifecycle review, revocation, and retirement. GA and preview controls, narrow eligibility, privacy, and authorization limits remain explicit.

rejected.reason: The package mixes generally available defensive features with preview or limited-access penetration testing, risk, shielding, and model capabilities, making a single availability claim misleading.
The initiative has not yet released a technical specification, conformance test, or delivery timetable and therefore does not establish an implemented governance control.

rejected.candidate: GitHub secret scanning, Copilot Evals, and Event Streams previews
rejected.reason: These are useful but opt-in, preview, waitlisted, product-local, or too early for a separate structural thesis.
The flow is operationally interesting but the announcement lacks a detailed threat model and outcome evidence sufficient for a separate signal.
The announcement depends on preview components and vendor assertions about accuracy, token use, and enterprise value without comparative production evidence.
Astra for Law and ChatGPT for Sales are extensions of the same model launch rather than independent technological signals.

rejected.reason: No additional primary-source item found before the cutoff met the exact-date, materiality, evidence, and deduplication threshold.

notes: Edition 40 proposes three traceable, moderate Signal Map movements: Models from capability-gated release infrastructure, AI Security from a governed remediation funnel, and Enterprise Adoption from cross-platform agent identity lifecycle evidence. No quantitative Signal Map score is used, and two accepted items update existing stories rather than duplicate them.
